intro: A draft model proposes tokens cheaply, while a target model verifies them. Rejection requires a corrected distribution, not ordinary target resampling.
task: Verify a supplied draft prefix, stopping at rejection and constructing the target-minus-draft correction distribution.
requirements: draft_probs and target_probs are same-shaped nonnegative (T,V) probability matrices with positive dimensions and row sums within 1e-8 of one; normalize each row by its sum before verification. tokens is a length-T integer vector of valid vocabulary indices.
uniforms is a length-T vector in [0,1). For each proposed token require positive draft probability. Accept while u < min(1,p_token/q_token); stop at the first rejection.

Return dict accepted as a Python token list, rejected_at as its first rejected index or -1, and correction as normalized max(p-q,0) for that row. If all tokens are accepted return an all-zero correction vector. This verifies a supplied prefix and does not generate a bonus token.

Numeric inputs must be real and finite with magnitude at most 1e30, except where a stricter bound is stated. Booleans are not numeric parameters. Leave all caller inputs unchanged and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Use the proposed token ratio
hints.body: Acceptance depends on target mass divided by draft mass at the proposed token.

hints.title: Correct for already-overproduced tokens
hints.body: The residual distribution keeps only positive target-minus-draft mass.

explanation: Acceptance reweights draft proposals toward the target distribution. On rejection, the residual distribution supplies probability mass the draft underrepresented.

The caller supplies probabilities conditioned on the appropriate prefix and reproducible uniform draws. This lesson isolates verification and leaves model execution, replacement sampling, and bonus-token generation outside the contract.
